title: Owning code unit and touched components per mention
description:
Split "which component" into one owning code unit and a list of touched datastores and third parties. Decision 4 of the parent initiative.

## Problem

In an internal dogfood scan, most files carried two asset components, usually a code unit and a datastore (an app plus its ORM). One pair of components carried identical locations. One "component" field cannot say both who owns a line and what the line talks to.

## Scope

- Owner: one code unit per file (an API service, a frontend app, a lambda, a docs site), from the file path and the scanner's sections (`getSectionIdFromProperties`, `src/core/sectioning/`). Detect and resolve components that carry identical location sets.
- Touches: a mention touches a datastore or third party when a `call` or `declaration` detection for it sits in the same scope, or when the call goes through a variable whose declaration came from that client (`const client = new Client(...)`).
- File-level `import` detections become touch candidates, not answers. Later tools may resolve them.

## Depends on

Scope spans and location kinds on detections.

## Done when

- Every mention record has exactly one owner or an explicit unknown.
- An email mention inside `sendWelcome()` next to `axios.post(` touches that component; a mention in a file that only imports a mailer SDK lists it as a candidate.
- No file in the corpus scans reports two owning code units.

## Evaluation

Owner and touches are asserted attributes on mention gold, scored only over gold that asserts them and only after the mention matches.
